Surah 58: Al-Mujadilah (The Pleading Woman)
[Medinan, and its verses are twenty-two]

﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of the woman who pleads with you (O Prophet)﴾ who argues with you, O Prophet, ﴿concerning her husband﴾ concerning her husband who had made her unlawful to himself (muzahir) by saying to her, "You are to me like the back of my mother," and she had asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about that, and he answered her that she had become unlawful to him, according to what was known among them, that zihar entails permanent separation. She was Khawlah bint Tha'labah, and her husband was Aws ibn al-Samit. ﴿And she complains to Allah﴾ of her loneliness and her poverty, and of her young children, who would be lost if she gathered them to him, or would go hungry if she gathered them to herself. ﴿And Allah hears your discussion﴾ your mutual exchange of words. ﴿Indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing﴾ knowing.

﴿Those who declare zihar﴾ (a pre-Islamic form of divorce in which a husband likens his wife to his mother). Its original form is يَتَظَهَّرُونَ (yatazahharūna), and the tā' was assimilated (idgham) into the ẓā'. In another reading there is an alif between the ẓā' and the light hā'. In another reading it is like يُقاتِلُونَ (yuqātilūna). The second occurrence is the same. ﴿from among you, from their wives; they are not their mothers; their mothers are only those who bore them﴾, read with a hamzah and a yā', and without a yā'. ﴿And indeed they say﴾, with the zihar, ﴿an objectionable word and a falsehood﴾, a lie. ﴿And indeed Allah is Most Pardoning, Most Forgiving﴾ to the one who commits zihar, when he pays the expiation (kaffārah).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 58, verse 3:

﴿And those who divorce by ẓihār from their wives and then wish to retract what they said﴾, i.e., to go back on it, by refraining from what the one who made ẓihār (ẓihār: the pre-Islamic pronouncement by which a husband declares his wife to be unlawful to him as his mother's back) has done with her, which is contrary to the purpose of ẓihār, namely describing the woman as forbidden; ﴿then the freeing of a slave﴾, i.e., manumitting one on his part ﴿before they touch one another﴾ by intercourse.

﴿Then whoever does not find [a slave]﴾ ﴿to free, then [he must observe] fasting for two consecutive months before they touch each other. Then whoever is not able﴾, i.e., to fast, ﴿then [he must provide] food for sixty needy people﴾. "Before they touch each other" also applies to it, i.e., before they touch each other. This is by applying the unrestricted (*mutlaq*, a general ruling not limited by conditions) to the restricted (*muqayyad*, a ruling limited by conditions), for each needy person one *mudd* (a standard measure) of the staple food of the land. ﴿That﴾, i.e., the leniency in the expiation (*kaffarah*, the atonement for certain sins), ﴿is so that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger. And these﴾, i.e., the aforementioned rulings, ﴿are the limits of Allah. And for the disbelievers﴾, i.e., those who disbelieve in them, ﴿is a painful torment﴾, i.e., distressing.

Indeed, those who oppose (yuhadduna) Allah and His Messenger ﴿يُحادُّونَ﴾ — they oppose (yukhalifuna) Allah and His Messenger — shall be humiliated (kubitu) ﴿كُبِتُوا﴾ — they shall be disgraced (udhillu) — ﴿كَما كُبِتَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلهمْ﴾ as those before them were humiliated, in their opposition to their messengers. ﴿وقَدْ أنْزَلْنا آيات بَيِّنات﴾ And We have certainly sent down clear signs, indicating the truthfulness of the Messenger. ﴿ولِلْكافِرِينَ﴾ And for the disbelievers, with respect to the signs, ﴿عَذاب مُهِين﴾ is a humiliating punishment, one that brings disgrace.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Tafsir al-Jalalayn), commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti on surah 58, verse 7:

﴿Have you not considered﴾ know: ﴿that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth. There is no secret conversation of three but that He is their fourth﴾, i.e., by His knowledge.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 58, verse 8:

﴿Have you not considered﴾ (tanzur, i.e., look) ﴿those who were forbidden secret consultation, then return to that which they were forbidden and consult together in sin, transgression, and disobedience to the Messenger﴾. They are the Jews. The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade them from their secret consultation (tanajji, i.e., speaking together in secret), looking at the believers so as to instill doubt into their hearts. ﴿And when they come to you﴾ O Prophet ﴿they greet you with that by which Allah does not greet you﴾, which is their saying: "As-sam ʿalayka" (i.e., death be upon you). ﴿And they say to themselves: "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?"﴾ (lawla, i.e., why not) for what we say of the greeting, and [they say] that he is not a prophet if he were a prophet. ﴿Hell is sufficient for them; they will burn therein, and wretched is the destination﴾, it is

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 58, verse 10:

﴿Indeed, secret counsel (al-najwa)﴾ is in sin and the like, i.e., the secret counsel in sin and the like, ﴿is from Satan﴾ through his deception, ﴿to grieve those who believe, but it does not harm them at all except by the permission of Allah﴾, i.e., His will.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 58, verse 11:

﴿O you who have believed, when you are told, "Make room" in the assemblies, then make room; Allah will make room for you.﴾ "Spread out" (تَوَسَّعُوا, tawassaʿū) ﴿in the assembly﴾, the assembly of the Prophet (ﷺ) and of remembrance, ﴿until whoever comes to you sits down.﴾ In another reading it is "the assemblies" (al-majālis). ﴿Then make room; Allah will make room for you﴾ in Paradise. ﴿And when you are told, "Rise up,"﴾ i.e., stand up ﴿to prayer and other good deeds, then rise up.﴾ In another reading the shin is vowelled with a ḍammah in both places (انْشُزُوا, unshuzū). ﴿Allah will raise those of you who have believed﴾ through obedience in this matter, ﴿and﴾ will raise ﴿those who have been given knowledge, by degrees﴾ in Paradise.

O you who have believed, when you consult the Messenger privately, (i.e., when you intend to confer with him privately), then present, before your private consultation, a charity (qabla-ha, i.e., before it), and (it is) purer for you (li-dhunubikum, i.e., for your sins). But if you do not find (anything that you can give in charity), then indeed Allah is Forgiving (li-munajatikum, i.e., for your private consultation) and Merciful to you (bikum). Meaning: there is no blame upon you in the private consultation without charity. Then it was abrogated (nasakha dhalika) by His saying:

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 58, verse 13:

﴿Are you apprehensive﴾ — with the two hamzas pronounced as they are (tahqiq), or with the second changed to an alif, or with the second eased (tashil) and an alif inserted between the eased one and the other; and with the hamza omitted (tark). That is: are you afraid ﴿that you should offer charity before your private consultation﴾ due to poverty? ﴿So since you did not do it﴾, i.e., the charity, ﴿and Allah has forgiven you﴾, i.e., turned back with you from it, ﴿then establish prayer, give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾, i.e., persist in that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 58, verse 14:

﴿Have you not seen﴾ (you should) look ﴿at those who have taken as allies﴾ (i.e., the hypocrites) ﴿a people﴾ (i.e., the Jews) ﴿with whom Allah is angry﴾ ﴿They are neither of you﴾ (i.e., the hypocrites are not) ﴿from among you﴾ (from among the believers) ﴿nor of them﴾ (from among the Jews); rather, they are wavering between the two ﴿and they swear to a lie﴾ (i.e., their claim) ﴿that they are believers, while they know﴾ that they are lying in it.
Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. Indeed, evil is what they used to do. [From the sins.]

﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾, a cover for themselves and their wealth, ﴿and so they barred﴾ the believers with them ﴿from the way of Allah﴾, meaning from jihad (striving in the way of Allah) against them, by killing them and seizing their wealth. ﴿For them is a humiliating punishment﴾, one that possesses humiliation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 58, verse 17:

﴿Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them anything against Allah﴾ (i.e., against His punishment) ﴿at all﴾ (i.e., of any avail)

﴿On the day Allah raises them all, then they swear to Him﴾ that they are believers ﴿as they swear to you, and they think that they have something﴾ of benefit from their oath ﴿in the Hereafter as in this world﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 58, verse 19:

﴿Istahwadha﴾ (istawla, "gained control") ﴿over them, Satan﴾ through their obedience to him ﴿so he made them forget the remembrance of God. Those are Satan's party﴾ (atbā'uh, "his followers").

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 58, verse 20:

﴿Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger⁠ — they will be among the most humbled.﴾ [Those who] oppose (يُخالِفُونَ) [Allah and His Messenger], [they are] among the most humbled (الأَذَلِّينَ), the defeated (المَغْلُوبِينَ).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 58, verse 21:

﴿Allah has decreed﴾ in the Preserved Tablet, or He has decided, ﴿"I will surely prevail, I and My messengers"﴾ by proof or by the sword.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 58, verse 22:

﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day befriending﴾ (yuṣādiqūn, i.e., they befriend) ﴿those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were﴾ (i.e., the opposers) ﴿their fathers﴾ (i.e., the believers) ﴿or their sons or their brothers or their kinsmen﴾ (rather, they intend them harm and fight them over faith, as happened to a group of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them). ﴿Those﴾ (those who do not befriend them) ﴿He has written﴾ (i.e., established) ﴿faith in their hearts, and strengthened them with a spirit﴾ (with a light) ﴿from Him﴾ (Exalted is He), ﴿and He will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein. Allah is pleased with them﴾ (by their obedience to Him) ﴿and they are pleased with Him﴾ (by His reward). ﴿Those are the party of Allah﴾ (they obey His command and avoid His prohibition). ﴿Surely the party of Allah are the successful﴾ (the winners).
